$comment: Compact number table . Snapshot of CLDR 48.2.3 decimalFormats-numberSystem-latn short (cldr-json cldr-numbers-full, fetched 2026-10-16) for the 16 app languages; quotes in patterns resolved, U+00A0 kept. Clients ship the same table in code and check it against this file; the platform ICU / Intl compact formatter is not used (Android CLDR follows the OS version).

source.numberingSystem: latn for every language, ar included

rules: Locale: drop everything from "@", replace "_" with "-", split on "-" keeping empty subtags (a leading "-" gives an empty language -> en), drop the first singleton subtag (one letter, e.g. -u- / -x-) and everything after it, compare subtags case-insensitively. zh: script first (Hans -> zh-Hans, Hant -> zh-Hant), else region TW / HK / MO -> zh-Hant, else zh-Hans; pt -> pt-BR; in (legacy Android Indonesian) -> id; other languages in the table by language subtag; anything else, empty included -> en.
Value: integer; negative counts as 0, above 10^15 counts as 10^15. value < 1000 -> plain ASCII digits, no grouping.
Tier: the last tier whose min <= value (values >= 10^12 use the 10^12 tier; the integer part may then exceed the pattern width and is not grouped).

Digits: z = length of the run of 0 in the pattern; unit = min / 10^(z-1); tenths = floor(value * 10 / unit) using integer arithmetic (unit / 10 is always an integer >= 100); int = tenths / 10, frac = tenths % 10. Always round down, never up.
Number text: int in ASCII digits, then decimal + frac when frac != 0 (".0" is dropped). Latin digits in every language.
Plural: a tier may carry "few" (only ar 1000). Use it when frac == 0 and int % 100 is 3...10; otherwise "pattern".

Pattern made of 0 only (zh-Hans / zh-Hant / ja 1000, de 1000 ... 100000): no abbreviation; the full value in ASCII digits, grouped with the group separator every 3 digits from the right only when value >= 10000 (ICU compact minimum grouping 2: 1234, 12.345).

Otherwise: replace the run of 0 in the pattern with the number text; everything else in the pattern is literal. No bidi marks are added; callers that embed the result in mixed-direction text isolate it.
